Declare input_producers exactly once: extraction={}, reasoning={facts:[refs]}, transformation={facts:[refs],expression:[one ref]}, verification={value:[one ref]} OR {facts:[refs],expression:[one ref]}. Every selected producer must provide a needed input: extraction supplies facts; reasoning requires extraction facts and produces expression; transformation requires BOTH facts and expression to calculate value; verification consumes EITHER a value OR facts+expression. All task question inputs are attached by program. Extraction MUST select context_field ctx_table or ctx_text. For arithmetic, identify ALL operands needed for the final goal across the actual source fields. Bind each necessary source into the final dependency chain; selecting only a deduction source while omitting its required starting quantity is incomplete. Do not add sources merely because they exist; irrelevant sources need no node. A unit-only source is insufficient. Check source_availability and actual task context, do not simply choose the last source. Use unique opaque semantic ref handles and descriptive name labels, not execution node IDs. The sole producer namespace is nodes[*].ref within THIS plan. A producer ref names a node, NEVER a fact ID, port, output instance, or execution ID. For node ref p, use facts:[\"p\"], NEVER p_facts_0 or p.value. Enumerate all refs first and check every producer against that exact set. Forward references are allowed. input_producers contains exact ref strings, including forward references; repeated names require distinct refs. The program allocates all execution IDs. Never add unnecessary verification or disconnected nodes. Every declared node must contribute through explicit input_producers to a final output. Node type selects its executable contract: a descriptive calculation name never turns extraction into calculation. Expressions are unevaluated syntax, not facts or numbers. Calculated and verified numbers may feed value ports, never facts ports. Do not merely move final_outputs to another isolated node; supply the task-required well-typed aggregation with explicit producers. Subtasks must describe the actual task, not contract IDs.
